items.title: Company directors not personally liable for unpaid legal fees: Bengaluru Court
items.summary: A Bengaluru civil court recently ruled in favour of law firm Krishnamurthy & Co. (K Law) in a suit seeking recovery of unpaid professional fees from Moerheim Roses and Trading India Private Limited, the Indian arm of a Dutch floriculture company. [K Law Vs Morheim Roses] In a judgment delivered on October 3, Additional City Civil and Sessions Judge Shirin Javeed Ansari directed the company to pay ₹2.75 lakh towards outstanding legal fees, along with interest at 9 percent per annum. However, the Court refused to hold the company's four directors personally liable for the dues. " The mere fact that a person is a director of a company does not, by itself, make such person personally liable for every contractual or commercial obligation of the company ," the Court observed. The dispute arose from legal services rendered by K Law in connection with a petition before the Karnataka High Court in 2017. According to the law firm, Moerheim Roses approached it through Delhi-based law firm Anand & Anand in January 2017. K Law subsequently filed objections, moved an application seeking vacation of an interim stay and engaged senior counsel to represent the company's interests. The firm raised invoices totalling ₹6.10 lakh, against which the company paid ₹3.35 lakh, leaving ₹2.75 lakh outstanding. Despite repeated reminders and a legal notice, the outstanding amount remained unpaid. K Law relied on email correspondence exchanged between 2021 and 2022 to establish that the company had acknowledged its liability and proposed payment arrangements. The firm eventually approached the civil court in November 2023, seeking recovery of the outstanding amount with interest at 24 percent per annum. The company and its directors failed to appear despite service of summons, following which the proceedings continued ex parte. The Court found that the invoices, payment records and evidence of appearances before the Karnataka High Court established the outstanding liability. However, it held that the directors could not be made personally responsible without evidence of an independent contractual undertaking or guarantee. items.summary: The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy ( MNRE ) issued an office memorandum on 23 rd July 2026, introducing the Model Service Agreement for “ Electrolyser as a Service ” ( EAAS ). This model agreement outlines industry standards for risk allocation, performance guarantees, and division of responsibilities. It aims to improve the ease of doing business and streamline the contract negotiations between green hydrogen project developers and the consumers. Under the model agreement, the Service Provider designs, constructs, owns, operates, and maintains an electrolytic hydrogen plant ( H2 Plant ) on a Build, Own, and Operate basis at the site provided by the Service Recipient. The Service Provider retains exclusive ownership, title, and operational control over the H2 Plant, with no tenancy or hire-purchase or financing or deferred sale rights created in favour of the Service Recipient. The Service Provider must secure necessary insurance for the H2 Plant. The Service Provider is also permitted to encumber the H2 Plant for financing purposes. In return, the Service Recipient pays monthly consideration covering product supply and plant’s O&M charges. This consideration can escalate annually based on the consumer price index for industrial workers published by the Department of Labour. The Service Recipient must provide milestone-based security deposits, and payment security via a revolving letter of credit. The Service Recipient is responsible for providing the site, managing civil works, maintaining green hydrogen certification, and providing utilities like water, power, nitrogen, sewerage and storage facilities. The Service Provider is responsible for the deployment and supervision of requisite personnel at the site, and ensuring compliance with employment laws. The Service Recipient cannot transfer or lease the site without the Service Provider's prior written consent. The standard contract term is 15 years from the commencement date and is extendable by mutual consent. If commissioning is delayed for reasons not caused by the Service Provider, it is treated as deemed commissioned triggering the Service Recipient's payment obligations. Additionally, the Service Provider must pass a performance guarantee test within 60 days of procurement of PESO license, failing which monthly payments stand suspended. items.title: CoC can't withdraw approved insolvency resolution plan citing debtor's improved financial position: Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday held that in corporate insolvency resolution proceedings, the Committee of Creditors (CoC) cannot withdraw an approved insolvency resolution plan merely by citing an improvement in the corporate debtor's financial position [ Bank of India & Ors. v. S.M. Kamal Pasha & Ors. ]. A Bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran held that a resolution plan becomes binding on both the CoC and the successful resolution applicant once it is approved by the creditors, even before its confirmation by the NCLT. The Court observed that the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 (IBC) does not permit either the CoC or the resolution applicant to withdraw from an approved resolution plan simply because subsequent developments have made the transaction financially less attractive. " We are of the opinion that the withdrawal of an application can only be till the CoC approves the plan and after it is placed before the Adjudicating Authority, there can be no withdrawal either of the application or the approved Resolution Plan," the October 26 judgment stated. The Court made the observation while dealing with a case concerning insolvency proceedings initiated by the Bank of India against a company engaged in toll collection on National Highway 45. During the Covid-19 pandemic, the company's financial position deteriorated, leading to the approval of a resolution plan involving ₹172.55 crore. At the time, the corporate debtor had an opening cash balance of approximately ₹30 crore. However, prolonged litigation delayed the implementation of the plan. During this period, the company's financial position improved considerably, with its opening cash balance increasing to approximately ₹165 crore. The CoC subsequently decided unanimously to withdraw its approval of the resolution plan and invite fresh expressions of interest. It argued that implementing the original plan would confer a windfall gain on the successful resolution applicant, who would effectively have to bring in significantly less money than originally contemplated. The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) permitted the withdrawal of the plan. However, the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT) later reversed that decision, holding that the CoC lacked the authority to withdraw its approval of the resolution plan. items.title: Minority judge blocked, Dhana's tactics, government's pre-approval: Justice SK Kaul reveals inner workings of Collegium
items.summary: The questionable working of the Supreme Court Collegium - the body responsible for appointing judges to the higher judiciary - has been laid bare by one of its former members and retired Supreme Court Justice Sanjay Kishan Kaul. In his memoirs titled Without Fear or Favour , the former judge most startlingly reveals that ex-Chief Justice of India (CJI) DY Chandrachud , as head of the Collegium, would seek the Central government's stance on potential appointments before consulting with the rest of the judges on the Collegium. The Collegium system was preserved by the Supreme Court in a bid to maintain judicial independence, free from executive influence. However, Justice Kaul seems to think that political considerations have long since crept, calling the method into question. In a scathing indictment of the system, he writes, "The collegium system worked well enough in the initial years, but over time, the judges have at times outdone the politicians. I have often been asked whether it is not altogether for the good that politicians have been excluded from the appointments process, and I have always replied to this slightly naive premise that ‘Judges ki rajneeti, rajnitigyon ki rajneeti ko mat kar deti hai. (The politics of the judges outdoes the politics of the politicians themselves.)’." CJI Chandrachud and pre-approval of government for judges' appointments Justice Kaul, who has known former CJI Chandrachud for over four decades, said that his relationship with the man he calls 'Dhana' had strained during his final years as a Supreme Court judge. He attributes this to one thing, more than others: "I believed he was too deferential to the government on appointment matters." He prefaces his opinion by saying that he was not one among those who believed that the government should not have any say in judicial appointments. He writes, "Total purdah cannot be the standard for independence, and blockages are bound to occur and do occur when consultation breaks down. But there is a difference between consultation and what I came to regard as pre-approval – seeking the government’s nod before the collegium had even formally deliberated. That sends the wrong signal. Any political class will always assert itself if you give them a wedge in the door. This is not in any sense a partisan matter but simply a question of the inevitable institutional dynamics of power." items.title: Theni jailbreak: 17 prisoners in TN escape after faking seizures, four of them caught
items.summary: The Tamil Nadu police have arrested four of the 17 remand prisoners who escaped from Thekkampatti sub-jail in Theni district on the night of Monday, October 26, after allegedly faking a medical emergency to draw prison staff into their cell and assaulting them. The first accused who was apprehended has been identified as Praveen Kumar. Three others — Silambarasan of Theni, and Raja Sikandar and Rajkumar, both from Madurai — were arrested during search operations in the early hours of October 27. Thirteen prisoners remain absconding, and police have launched a statewide search to trace them. According to preliminary investigations, all 17 prisoners were lodged in the same cell. At around 10.30 pm on October 26, some of them allegedly called the prison staff on duty, claiming that one of the inmates was suffering from epileptic seizures and needed medical assistance. When the prison staff opened the cell and entered to help, the inmates allegedly attacked them and fled the area at around 11 pm. Grade II police constable Thangapandi, who was among the personnel attacked, sustained a head injury and was admitted to Theni Government Medical College and Hospital. Two other prison staff members also sustained injuries and were undergoing treatment. The Theni district police deployed 17 special teams to trace the escaped prisoners. Checkposts have been strengthened across Theni and neighbouring districts, with vehicle checks intensified at major routes, bus stands and railway stations. Dindigul Superintendent of Police S Jeyakumar told the media that checkposts had been established at 16 locations in the neighbouring districts as a precautionary measure. Police in Madurai and Kerala have also been alerted, and photographs of the escaped prisoners have been circulated to help identify them. Search operations have extended to forest areas along the Western Ghats and the neighbouring Idukki district in Kerala. Police are also monitoring routes through which the escapees may have returned to their hometowns. Preliminary reports suggest that many of the escaped accused are from Madurai, Ramanathapuram, Salem and Villupuram districts. Following the incident, some of the other prisoners held at the sub-jail were shifted to Madurai Central Prison. Theni Superintendent of Police KS Praveen Gowtham inspected the spot, while Kandamanur police registered a case and began further investigation. items.title: Bengaluru Police arrest three men for killing man in road rage attack
items.summary: Bengaluru’s Electronics City police have arrested three men for allegedly running over a 25-year-old man and dragging him beneath their car for around 100 to 150 metres, following a road altercation in Bengaluru. The victim, Ranjith Kumar Sahu, who was killed in the incident, was a native of Bihar working as a cook at a paying guest accommodation in BTM Layout. A fourth accused, identified as Shyam Kohar, remains absconding. The arrested men are Ajay Rabidas (26), Sajal Namasudra (19), and Bijoy Ray (27), all natives of Assam. The incident occurred around 1.50 am on October 21 near Pragathipura, within the limits of Electronics City police station. According to a complaint filed by Sahu’s friend, Nitish Kumar Mukhiya, a car approached their group at high speed as they were crossing the road after celebrating Dasara. When Mukhiya signalled the driver to slow down, the occupants allegedly took offence, made a U-turn and returned to confront the group. The confrontation escalated into an argument and an assault, following which Mukhiya called Sahu, who was at a nearby residence. When Sahu arrived, the altercation intensified, according to the complaint. The occupants allegedly attempted to flee in their car while Sahu was standing in front of the vehicle. The driver accelerated, hitting Sahu and dragging him beneath the car for around 100 to 150 metres, the complaint said. The occupants then allegedly pulled Sahu from beneath the vehicle, abandoned him near the Hosur service road and fled. He sustained serious injuries to his head, chest, right leg and other parts of his body. He was taken to a private hospital in Madiwala, where he died on October 22. Police identified the suspects after examining CCTV footage and recording statements from witnesses and local residents. Deputy Commissioner of Police (Electronics City) M Narayana said the footage did not clearly capture the car, but enquiries with residents, particularly people running roadside eateries through the night, helped investigators identify the vehicle and trace the suspects. Technical assistance also helped solve the case, he said. Police investigation indicated that Rabidas was driving the car at the time of the incident. The accused reportedly told investigators that they had been heavily intoxicated after a party. Police are continuing efforts to trace Kohar, the fourth accused.
